note: Quarter fully pre-released by the 14 Oct trading update; a one-off impairment reversal headline is sold, the FY guide can only narrow toward the lower half, and the stock ran +13% in 20 sessions into a print that adds nothing to the quarter.

The >EUR36m EBITDA guide needs a 12.5% H2 margin against 4.7% in H1 on hardware-heavy mix (primary documents), a decisive shortfall on a 91%-vol name whose last FY print fell 23.8%; the investigator's conclusions are a two-sided tail leaning clean, and the EUR1bn ambition carries a pre-hedged delay caveat; window is likely amc (close 10-29 to close 10-30).

Demant's +6-7% Q3 market read makes the '>3%' organic guide look conservative and firming has been bought this year, but the 9 Oct rally and the MS whisper above consensus already hold most of it and the Q3 comp is two points tougher; amc release, window close 10-29 to close 10-30.

Revenue is pre-released so the move is in adj. EBIT and a stale 'mid single digit' LFL outlook against 12.2% actual; a lift is plausible but the stock is +19% in 20 sessions to within 8-10% of all three broker targets with no sourced EBIT bar, so the run-up offsets most of it.

Volumes and prices are pre-released and the +27% run-up tracks Brent, so the only unpriced lines are net debt and the dividend; the USD 396m Capricorn cash now sits unspent into the first dividend decision since, where raises moved the stock about 9% twice, but a hold is the base case.

A cash shell at about 3x its own NOK 0.80-1.00 retained-cash estimate, bid up 11% in five sessions on nothing, meets its first report with hard NAV numbers and no scheduled strategic update; the upside tail is a named counterparty, which no filing or flow shows leaking; the run-up control is a dividend artefact here.

Q2 actuals, the usual Q3 margin step-up and a full quarter of the May headcount savings point to adj. EBITDA above the 14.7 consensus column, profitability beats were bought on the last four prints, and the stock is flat on $258k a day; the bar is disputed (Inderes already at 15.3), which caps the size, and a 4.88% exiting holder sits on the book.

Seasonal arithmetic on the company's own quarterly table puts Q3 EBIT at 81-85 against an 86-89 consensus that SHB has pushed higher still, on a name that fell 9.8% and 13.0% on its last two margin misses, against a hard +31% order comp; Volvo CE's raised European forecast is the positive offset and is partly in the 26 Oct bounce.

SSB's NACE 47.19 value index, which has tracked the Europris chain within a point for five quarters, reads -0.3% for Q3 against a +9.5% comp (September published the morning before the print), implying flat Norwegian sales and deleverage on a name that fell on 9 of 12 results days and ran +4.6% into this one; the NOK gross-margin tailwind is mostly modelled.

Pool Corp (+4%, accelerating, inventory -3%), Hayward (NA +9%, early-buy ahead, guide raised) and Pentair (channel realignment complete) all printed 22-28 Oct and rose 12-14% while FDR gained about 4%, so the North American read-through is only partly in the price on a name whose last two Q3 prints rose 7.1% and 9.4%.

H1 EBIT of 316m leaves only ~384m for H2 against a 198m Q2, so the >700m guide has room, but the new team has parked targets for the 25 Nov CMD and the stock is +8.9% under a 65-66 resistance; the frozen VAC contract and restructuring costs are small drags on a print with no sourced Q3 bar.

The company's own H1 quarters put FY adj. net profit 1-5% above the top of the 740-760m guide, Italgas raised at the 9M stage last year (+4.2% vs Snam flat), and the stock has de-rated 11 points against Snam since July, so a raise or 'above' wording is more likely than not and only partly priced; a low-vol utility caps the size.

Margin is the line this name trades on (-6.8%, -18.3%, -12.1% on the last three misses) and none of Q2's stated margin drags is declared over, with Pareto dropping it from its October portfolio on 'may disappoint'; the NOK 11.5bn of disclosed Q3 orders is known and the Belgium pop was given back, so the order rebound is worth less than the margin risk.

TotalEnergies' Q3 refining marker at 33.2 $/bbl plus Neste's 5-12 $/bbl historical premium implies 39-45 against the ~36 in consensus, and Enilive's biorefining EBIT +39% QoQ landed after the Vara snapshot, on a stock already down 18% from its high; the RP volume-guide trim and cautious Q4 wording are the real tails, and DGD's margin collapse is a partial US read.

An OMIE quarter at ~124 EUR/MWh against ~67 a year ago favours Naturgy's CCGT-heavy book and leaves a guide raise possible, but Endesa's same-day print implies Q3 EBITDA -12% with a Q4 warning, so the two transmissions roughly cancel on a low-vol name.

Transport Fever 3's record launch two days before quarter-end and a possible Playrion disposal gain sit against a 105 MSEK EBIT bar that is already below last year on a stock down 10.7% in 20 sessions; the cost line (SHB's launch-dilution cut, Q2's 7.6% EBIT miss) is the main risk and EBIT decides the sign here.

The 19.1 MEUR consensus asks for +2.0m y/y against +0.8m in Q2 while Inderes, the closest follower, sits at 18 on the margin, and the stock has followed the sign of the EBIT surprise on all four observed prints; after +27% in 60 days it trades at or above every target but one, so an in-line print has no room.

Whitbread and IHG put UK RevPAR up 2.8-3.2% through the concert comp, which mostly confirms August's 'continue to perform strongly', while Croatian overnights were flat through Arena's peak season; good UK numbers were sold on the last two prints, so a trading update with the FY reiterated nets to little.

Rx Germany and the margin are pre-released and the 28 Sep guide implies a Q4 slowdown that a third raise could correct against a 4.28% short, but the first unseen line is non-Rx, which Redcare's own 'softer July' and DocMorris's OTC +3.5% say slowed, and a new CEO's first call after a +33% run-up has faded before (+2.1% then -6.6% after the Q2 raise was out).

The Q4 guide against ~$4.09bn decides a print whose confirmed results-day median is about 13% with 7 of 9 down; NXP's above-seasonal Q4 guide and TI's flat one support at-or-above consensus but NXPI fell on its own print and STMPA did not outperform on 28 Oct, so the sign is near even and the size is the baseline's 3.85% understated by three.
